stem.en: A mould under a microscope shows long threads, a round sac on a thread, and tiny round bodies in the sac. Which naming is right?

text.en: The threads are spores; the sac is a hypha.

feedback.en: Spores are the tiny round bodies. The threads are hyphae.

text.en: The threads are buds; the tiny bodies inside are seeds.

feedback.en: Moulds make no seeds, and hyphae are not buds.

text.en: The threads are hyphae; the tiny bodies are spores.

feedback.en: Yes. Hyphae are the threads, and the sac at the tip holds the spores.

text.en: The threads are roots; the sac is a tiny fruit.

feedback.en: Moulds are fungi. They have no roots or fruits like a plant.

explanation.en: Hyphae are the long threads. A sporangium is the round sac on a thread. The spores inside it can each grow into a new individual.

hints.en: Which part is small enough to float in air?
